subject: Pilot model shortlist & next steps — latency / cost / quality tradeoffs
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.inference>
To: Aditi Mehra <aditi@nimbusanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-04-18T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot model shortlist & next steps — latency / cost / quality tradeoffs

Hi Aditi / Ankit,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — appreciate the candor on throughput targets and the 95th %-ile latency requirement (<120ms for short replies). Per our conversation I pulled together a pragmatic shortlist and a proposed pilot evaluation plan so we can converge quickly on the right candidate(s). Attached: a condensed benchmark summary, the prompt set we'll run for quality, and raw latency samples from our lab runs.

High-level recommended shortlist (order = priority):
- RW-Base-Mid (fp16) — balanced quality, predictable latency (90–130ms typical on our DaVinci-8 GPU pool), moderate token cost. Great baseline for semantic search + short generation.
- RW-Lite-Quant (4-bit) — lowest per-token cost and best tail latency for bursty traffic (60–100ms), slight drop on long-form summarization and rare-entity fidelity; good candidate where cost is the primary constraint.
- Open-M70-Large (fp16) — highest quality on long-context summarization and instruction follow-through, but higher cost and latency (150–240ms); use as canary / fallback for high-quality requests.

Why this mix: it gives you a predictable baseline (RW-Base-Mid), a cost-optimized variant for volume (RW-Lite-Quant), and a high-quality fallback (Open-M70-Large). We can run parallel A/B evaluations on your 5k example prompts and report token-level cost, per-case diff in Rouge/BLEU-like metrics, and latency percentiles.

Open questions / asks (please confirm in reply):
1) Finalize pilot dataset (you mentioned 5k sample prompts + 200 labeled gold answers) — can you confirm delivery by EOD Thu?
2) Are there any security/allowed-PII constraints beyond what we discussed (HIPAA or EU residency)?
3) Desired success criteria for the pilot (acceptable cost per 1k requests, min quality thresholds).

Next steps I propose:
- You deliver the sample set.
- We run a 72-hour synthetic load + deterministic eval (we'll share a dashboard).
- Joint review and selection of the production candidate and rollout policy (canary %, cache rules, quantization lock).

I'll coordinate the evaluation work with Marissa and Karthik — copying them for ops + eval specifics.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: benchmark_summary_20270418.pdf, prompt_set_v2.json, latency_samples_q2.csv
From: Aditi Mehra <aditi@nimbusanalytics.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.inference>
Cc: Ankit Rao <ankit@cloudops.nimbus.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot model shortlist & next steps — latency / cost / quality tradeoffs

Diego,

Thanks — this is really helpful and aligns with what we discussed. Quick clarifications:  
- We'll deliver the 5k prompt set by Thursday EOD PST (I asked engineering to prioritize).
- No HIPAA or EU residency requirements for the pilot; all traffic is US-only for now.
- Success criteria: average cost per 1k requests < $12 and final quality delta vs. our baseline model should be >= +6% on our composite score.

Two asks from our side:
1) How will Redwood detect quality regressions during the pilot? We need a pre-configured dashboard and alerting if our composite drops >4% from the baseline during a rolling 24h window.
2) Can the fallback (to Open-M70-Large) be automated based on a confidence threshold, or will we need manual failover?

Appreciate the fast turnaround — looking forward to the eval results.

— Aditi
Aditi Mehra
Head of ML Products, Nimbus Analytics
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.inference>, Aditi Mehra <aditi@nimbusanalytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-04-18T18:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot model shortlist & next steps — latency / cost / quality tradeoffs

Aditi — quick note on the monitoring and automation asks.

Monitoring / regression detection:
- We'll run the 5k labeled set through the candidate models and populate a short-term quality dashboard (Drive link included in related links).
- We'll surface a composite score (precision / recall / semantic-similarity weighted) and wire a threshold rule: alert if rolling 24h composite drops >4% vs. baseline. Alerts can push to your SRE Slack channel or email; we can also add PagerDuty for production rollouts.

Automated fallback policy options (pick one):
A) Confidence-based auto-fallback: Redwood evaluates a model-level confidence proxy (likelihood ratio + token-entropy heuristic). If confidence < threshold, we transparently route the request to the Open-M70-Large fallback. This adds ~120–180ms to those specific requests.
B) Canary-first manual: start with canary traffic at 10% to the candidate model; human review for edge failures, then escalate automation after 72h.

Recommendation: start with option B for the pilot (safer) and enable option A once we validate the confidence signal on the labeled set. We'll include the confidence metric in the evaluation outputs.

Operational notes:
- We'll collect per-request tokens and cost estimates using Redwood Console and provide a per-route cost dashboard.
- We'll export the raw evals to the Drive folder and include a CSV with per-example diffs so you can review failure modes.

Marissa
Director, Model Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>, Aditi Mehra <aditi@nimbusanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot model shortlist & next steps — latency / cost / quality tradeoffs

Adding a pragmatic eval / rollout checklist so we can move quickly: 

1) Pilot dataset acceptance (Aditi) — deliver by Thu EOD.
2) Baseline run (Redwood) — run all three candidates on the labeled set + 72h synthetic load to capture tail latency. Deliverable: benchmark CSV + sample traces.
3) Quality review session (joint) — 60-minute sync to review top 50 failures and alignment to your composite metric.
4) Cost projection — we will provide a 30-day projected cost at expected QPS and an estimated per-1k cost table.
5) Rollout policy — default: 10% canary for 48h -> 50% for 24h -> full if metrics hold; enable cache and KV prefix for common prompts to reduce unit cost.

I'll own steps 2 and 4. Marissa will own monitoring and the confidence metric. Diego will coordinate scheduling with Nimbus.

Also attaching a short eval matrix (see attached prompt_set_v2.json and benchmark_summary_20270418.pdf) — we'll populate the Drive sheet with the results as soon as the runs complete.

Karthik
Head of Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.inference>
To: Aditi Mehra <aditi@nimbusanalytics.com>

Subject: Re: Pilot model shortlist & next steps — latency / cost / quality tradeoffs

Perfect — thanks all. Aditi, looks like we're aligned on the pilot scope and the success criteria. Recap of agreed actions and owners: 

- Nimbus (Aditi): deliver 5k prompts + 200 labeled gold answers by 2027-04-22 EOD PST.
- Redwood (Karthik): run candidate benchmarks + 72h synthetic load; deliver results and cost projection by 2027-04-24.
- Redwood (Marissa): configure regression alerts and confidence proxy; share alert rules and dashboard by 2027-04-24.
- Joint: 60-minute quality review the day after results are shared (suggest Tue 2027-04-26).

If that timeline works I will open the HubSpot deal stage update and attach the evaluation docs to the record. We'll keep the fallback policy set to canary-first for the pilot and table auto-fallback until confidence is validated.

Thanks — will ping once the runs start.

Diego
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
